long.title: Will Young: Two Innings in One | India vs New Zealand - 4th ODI
long.description:
India vs New Zealand, 4th ODI analysis at Bay Oval, Mount Maunganui: New Zealand 333. India 89 all out. A 244-run defeat at Mount Maunganui. We took every ball of the 4th ODI (line, length, shot played, and whether the batter was in control) to work out who decided it and why: Matt Henry's triple-wicket first over, Will Young's 125 and the two lives that started it, and the middle overs where India lost the grip.

Sources: ball-by-ball data from ESPNcricinfo and Cricbuzz match pages (captured with our own tool, cross-checked over by over); result and Player of the Match from both. All numbers are computed by us from the ball data; 'not in control' is the Cricinfo shot-control flag. All graphics are original, not broadcast footage.

short.vo: A hundred and twenty-five off a hundred and eight balls. Will Young's innings was really two innings.
In his first fifty balls, he was not in control on fifteen of them.
In the second over he was dropped twice, off consecutive balls. He had five.
Then he took over. Balls fifty-one to seventy-five: just two false shots, thirty-five runs.
A hundred and twenty of his hundred and twenty-five came after those two lives. Follow for the full breakdown.
